title: The Formula for Agentic AI Value
gist: BCG's 2026 Applied AI Index (1,300+ CxOs) finds nearly half of companies now generate AI value, with the 7.5% 'future-built' leaders showing 2.4x top-line growth and 5x AI value by combining strategic clarity with applied AI. AI spend has tripled to 3.3% of revenue, agentic AI's share of value is set to rise from 22% to 39% by 2030, yet only 5% of firms have agent controls in place.

insights.claim: In BCG's 2026 Applied AI Index (survey of 1,300+ CxOs across 20+ sectors), almost 50% of companies now generate value from AI: 7.5% are future-built, 41% scaling, 47% emerging and 4.5% stagnating.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Counters the 'AI isn't paying off' narrative that weighs on AI capex sentiment.
insights.quote: Nearly half of companies are capturing value from AI, overturning the idea that enterprise AI isn’t paying off.
insights.locator: How many companies are actually getting value from AI?

insights.claim: The most AI-mature 7.5% of companies (future-built) show 2.4 times the top-line growth of companies in the bottom half of the sample.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: AI maturity is becoming a measurable driver of revenue dispersion between winners and laggards within sectors.
insights.quote: they show 2.4 times as much top-line growth as companies in the bottom half of our sample
insights.locator: Enterprise AI is starting to deliver.

insights.claim: Companies that score well on both strategic clarity and applied AI generate five times as much value from AI as those that prioritize neither, which BCG calls the clearest evidence yet of the magnitude of AI returns in practice.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Execution quality, not mere AI adoption, determines returns; screen for firms with coherent, C-suite-owned AI programs.
insights.quote: generate five times as much value from AI as companies that don’t prioritize strategic clarity and applied AI
insights.locator: Transformative Impact.

insights.claim: When companies scale AI in a core workflow, such as credit decisioning in banking, claims-fraud detection in insurance, or demand forecasting in consumer goods, they generate double-digit gains in productivity, revenue and cost reduction for those workflows.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Identifies specific high-ROI use cases likely to show up first in margins of financials and consumer companies.
insights.locator: The payoff shows up in every industry.

themes.theme: AI spending surge and where it sits

insights.claim: AI spending has more than tripled in two years, rising from about 1% of revenue in early 2025 to 3.3% of revenue today.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Enterprise AI budgets at 3.3% of revenue imply a large and fast-growing demand pool for AI software, services and infrastructure.
insights.quote: AI spending has more than tripled in two years, from about 1% of revenue in early 2025 to 3.3% today.
insights.locator: Does spending more on AI make companies better at it?

insights.claim: Across all surveyed companies, 80% of AI spending sits outside enterprise IT budgets.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Vendors selling to business units rather than CIOs capture most AI budget; go-to-market matters for AI software names.
insights.quote: Across all companies surveyed, 80% of AI spending sits outside enterprise IT.
insights.locator: Does spending more on AI make companies better at it?

insights.claim: Spending more on AI does not by itself make companies better at it; future-built companies are 3.5 times more likely than laggards to fund a single multiyear program (61% versus 17%) and concentrate on fewer, higher-value workflows.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Capital allocation discipline around AI, not budget size, is the differentiator to look for in management commentary.
insights.quote: future-built companies are 3.5 times more likely than laggards to fund a single multiyear program (61% versus 17%)
insights.locator: Does spending more on AI make companies better at it?

insights.claim: Companies tracking AI value directly in the P&L realize three times the AI value of companies that do not formally measure it (3.6% versus 1.2%), and 95% of future-built companies measure AI via the P&L or KPIs.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Firms disclosing P&L-linked AI metrics are more likely to be genuine AI value creators.
insights.quote: those tracking directly in the P&L realize three times the AI value of companies that do not formally measure it—3.6% versus 1.2%
insights.locator: How should companies measure the returns of AI?

themes.theme: Agentic AI as next value pool

insights.claim: Agentic AI's share of total AI value rose from 17% in the 2025 sample to 22% in the 2026 sample and is on track to reach 39% by 2030.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Value is migrating toward agent platforms and orchestration; supports demand for agent-ready infrastructure and software.
insights.quote: The agentic share of total AI value has already climbed from 17% in the 2025 sample to 22% in the 2026 sample, and it is on track to reach 39% by 2030.
insights.locator: Shift to an AI-first operating model

insights.claim: 44% of future-built companies already realize value from agentic AI, versus only 2% of laggards.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Agentic value is extremely concentrated among leaders, widening competitive gaps.
insights.quote: 44% of future-built companies say that they already realize value from agentic AI today, whereas very few laggards (2%) do
insights.locator: Shift to an AI-first operating model

insights.claim: 42% of companies expect their AI agents to act autonomously, deciding without human approval, by 2030, yet only 5% have the relevant agent controls in place.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: A large governance gap signals demand for agent control, security and observability tooling and potential risk incidents.
insights.quote: 42% of companies expect their agents to act autonomously by 2030, deciding without human approval, and just 5% have the relevant agent controls in place
insights.locator: How do companies keep control of AI agents

insights.claim: Companies with all six AI controls in place across the enterprise generate three times as much agentic AI value as companies with just one control, implying risk controls enable rather than restrain agentic value.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: AI governance spend is value-accretive; bullish for vendors of AI risk, control-plane and guardrail tooling.
insights.quote: companies with all six AI controls in place across the enterprise generate three times as much agentic AI value as companies with just one control
insights.locator: Shift to an AI-first operating model

insights.claim: BCG advises putting agent controls in place before granting autonomy, arguing that sustaining agentic AI value is a matter of governance and not only technology.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Companies scaling agents without governance face elevated operational and reputational risk.
insights.quote: Put the controls in before you grant autonomy.
insights.locator: How do companies keep control of AI agents

insights.claim: Companies expect a workforce reduction of roughly 10% to 15% from AI, yet 89% expect AI to generate new work and only 11% expect it mainly to replace existing jobs.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Implies meaningful but not catastrophic labor displacement; supports productivity gains with partial headcount offsets.
insights.quote: companies expect a workforce reduction of roughly 10% to 15% from AI, yet 89% expect AI to generate new work
insights.locator: Will agentic AI cut or change jobs?

insights.claim: Strategic workforce planning for which roles should exist in an agentic world is practiced by 55% of future-built companies versus 17% of laggards.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Organizational readiness is a leading indicator of which firms will convert AI spend into returns.
insights.locator: Reinvent the workforce around humans and agents.

insights.claim: BCG's 10-20-70 model holds that AI transformation effort should be 10% algorithms, 20% technology and data, and 70% changes to people, organization and processes.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Bulk of AI transformation value accrues via change management and services, not models alone; supportive of consulting/services demand.
insights.quote: In BCG’s 10-20-70 model, 10% of the effort should go into the algorithms, and 20% into the technology and data.
insights.locator: The Playbook: How to Become an Agentic

insights.claim: The technology gap that now shapes company performance lies in an agent-ready AI platform with enterprise intelligence and platform layers that let agents understand context, take governed action and run reliably at scale.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Spending focus is shifting from models to enterprise platform and data layers.
insights.locator: Build an agentic platform powered by data.

insights.claim: 95% of future-built companies are undergoing a data transformation, and more than two-thirds are committing to a single enterprise-wide AI platform with a common architecture and control plane rather than a single-vendor stack.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Leaders favor vendor-neutral platforms over single-vendor stacks, a headwind for lock-in strategies and tailwind for data/control-plane players.
insights.quote: more than two-thirds are committing to a single enterprise-wide AI platform with a common architecture and control plane, instead of a single-vendor stack
insights.locator: Build an agentic platform powered by data.

insights.claim: Among ten highlighted sectors, technology pairs the highest applied AI maturity with the strongest realized value, while machinery and chemicals lag on both strategic clarity and applied AI with modest realized impact.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Industrial sectors have the most AI upside still unrealized; tech already captures the most value.
insights.quote: Technology pairs the highest applied AI maturity with the strongest realized value among ten highlighted sectors.
insights.locator: Technology

insights.claim: Banking combines high AI maturity and bold AI investment with cost gains running ahead of revenue impact, while telecommunications leads on strategic clarity but has more modest realized value, particularly on revenue.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: AI benefits in banks show up as cost efficiency first; telecom AI revenue upside is lagging.
insights.quote: Banking combines high AI maturity with bold AI investment, while cost gains run ahead of revenue impact.
insights.locator: Banking

insights.claim: Retail reports relatively strong realized AI value on both revenue and cost despite comparatively low AI spending.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: Retail shows high AI capital efficiency, a potential margin tailwind.
insights.quote: Retail reports relatively strong realized value on both revenue and cost, alongside comparatively low AI spending.
insights.locator: Retail

insights.claim: BCG argues that sector, legacy and starting point do not determine AI destiny; leadership choices do, and every one of the 20+ sectors analyzed contains at least one future-built or scaling organization.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/jessica-apotheker
insights.so_what: AI winners can emerge within any sector, so stock-picking within sectors matters more than sector bets on AI.
insights.quote: Sector, legacy, and starting point do not determine destiny; leadership choices do.
insights.locator: The evidence from our analysis is encouraging
